CHIEF COMPLAINT
Big toe pain and redness for two weeks, worsening over the past week.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports intermittent big toe pain for approximately two weeks, with significant worsening over the past week. Pain became severe during a trade show convention last week, limiting his ability to walk the halls. He describes the pain as throbbing in nature with occasional sharp, stabbing quality, especially with movement or prolonged walking. Patient compensates by walking on his heel to avoid bending the toe. He denies a specific injury but notes onset of redness and warmth to touch, which prompted him to seek care. Pain is exacerbated by light pressure, including bed sheets at night. He reports taking ibuprofen 200 mg twice daily without significant relief. Denies symptom improvement with current management. Riding a bike does not bother the toe as he pedals with the back of his feet on regular pedals while wearing flip-flops most of the time.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports pain with light pressure to the big toe, including discomfort from bed sheets at night. Denies injury. Pain worsens with movement and weight-bearing activities.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

MEDICATIONS
Ibuprofen 200 mg twice daily.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is on his feet daily for work. He enjoys biking on trails (over 800 miles last year on regular pedals in flip-flops) and fishing. He enjoys spicy Mexican food.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Big toe joint examination reveals: Pain with range of motion testing, particularly with plantar flexion (10-20 degrees). Joint demonstrates limited dorsiflexion with less pain. Pain with medial-lateral motion of the first metatarsophalangeal joint with grinding sensation noted. Tenderness with palpation between the first and second toes (mild) and on the lateral aspect of the first metatarsophalangeal joint (significant). Small bone spur palpated over the joint.

RESULTS
X-ray of the foot reveals a large bone spur on the top of the big toe joint and significant cartilage loss consistent with arthritis of the first metatarsophalangeal joint.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Hallux rigidus with degenerative joint disease of the first metatarsophalangeal joint.
Plan: 1) Initiate orthotic insert for shoe. 2) Start meloxicam once daily for anti-inflammatory management. Patient counseled regarding potential gastrointestinal side effects (heartburn or epigastric pain); instructed to discontinue medication and call if these symptoms develop. 3) Continue regular work and activities to assess treatment effectiveness. 4) Follow-up appointment in two weeks to assess response to conservative treatment. If no significant improvement, consider more invasive options including corticosteroid injection or surgical intervention (joint cleaning or arthrodesis). Patient to avoid time off work during this trial period.
